record_scope_reconstruction: Five formal Ecuador road crossings have different reopening histories. Macará and Lalamor vehicles resume July7/8 after earlier pedestrian allowance; SanMiguel retains permitted exceptions; LaBalsa and Jimbura still closed at July17 report.

source_checks.finding: December26 report describes December24 Macará closure while Rumichaca/Huaquillas retained, with Loja–Piura transport affected.
Loja government July4 notice explicitly reopens pedestrian access, not ordinary vehicle traffic.
July9 on-site report dates Lalamor bridge pedestrian/vehicle flow to July8 about13:40 and Macará to July7 night.
April1 report locates SanMiguel blockade at CEBAF3km before bridge; special permits and crude movement exceptions remain. Informal river routes are separate.
July17 report distinguishes still-closed LaBalsa and Jimbura bridges from reopened Macará/Lalamor.
Named ControlMacara border node adjacent to customs and migration,3km southwest of Macará town; not town centre. Exact bridge closure barrier not independently located.
Named PuenteInternacionalAlamor adjacent to ElAlamor Peruvian control and Lalamor Ecuador customs170m east; identity matches July8 Lalamor reopening report.
Explicit named CEBAF office south of river. Original Ecuavisa report places closure at CEBAF about3km before bridge; office coordinate represents control complex, not bridge or precise barrier.
Named Peru frontier-police station next to migration and border barrier, with Ecuador immigration150m north. Partial route reference; Ecuador bridge barrier not directly mapped.
